name: GO Classes CS | Discrete Mathematics | Functions | Weekly Quiz 12

question.text:
Let $\mathrm{X}$ be a finite set. Suppose $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{X}$ is a function. Which of the following are possible?

  1. $\mathrm{f}$ is injective but not surjective.
     
  2. $\mathrm{f}$ is surjective but not injective.
     
  3. $\mathrm{f}$ is surjective and injective.
     
  4. f is neither surjective nor injective.
Consider the function $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ given recursively by $f(0)=1$ and $f(n+1)=2 \cdot f(n)$. Find $f(10)$.

Let $\mathrm{g}: \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}$ be functions. If $\mathrm{f} \circ \mathrm{g}$ is bijective, then which of the following must be true?

  1. $g$ is one to one.
     
  2. $g$ is onto.
     
  3. $f$ is one to one.
     
  4. $\mathrm{f}$ is onto.

Suppose $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{Y}$ is a function. Which of the following are possible?

  1. $f$ is injective but not surjective.
     
  2. $f$ is surjective but not injective.
     
  3. $f$ is surjective and injective.
     
  4. $\mathrm{f}$ is neither surjective nor injective.

Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$. Let $h = g \circ f : X \to Z$. Suppose $g$ is one-to-one and onto. Which of the following is FALSE?

  1. If $f$ is one-to-one then $h$ is one-to-one and onto.
     
  2. If $f$ is not onto then $h$ is not onto.
     
  3. If $f$ is not one-to-one then $h$ is not one-to-one.
     
  4. If $f$ is one-to-one then $h$ is one-to-one.

The following functions all have $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ as both their domain and codomain. Which of the following is both injective \& surjective?
 

  1. $f=\left(\begin{array}{lllll}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3\end{array}\right)$.
     
  2. $f=\left(\begin{array}{lllll}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 & 5 & 4\end{array}\right)$.
     
  3. $f(x)=6-x$.
     
  4. $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}x / 2 & \text { if } x \text { is even } \\ (x+1) / 2 & \text { if } x \text { is odd }\end{array}\right.$.

The functions mapping $R$ into $R$ are defined as :

$f\left(x \right)=x^{3} - 4x, g\left(x \right)=\frac{1}{x^{2}+1}$ and $h\left(x \right)=x^{4}.$

Then find the value of the following composite functions :

$h_{o}g\left(x \right)$ and $h_{o}g_{o}f\left(x \right)$

  1. $\left ( x^{2}+1 \right )^{4}$ and $\left [ \left ( x^{3}-4x \right )^{2}+1 \right ]^{4}$
        
  2. $\left ( x^{2}+1 \right )^{4}$ and $\left [ \left ( x^{3}-4x \right )^{2}+1 \right ]^{-4}$
     
  3. $\left ( x^{2}+1 \right )^{-4}$ and $\left [ \left ( x^{2}-4x \right )^{2}+1 \right ]^{4}$
     
  4. $\left ( x^{2}+1 \right )^{-4}$ and $\left [ \left ( x^{3}-4x \right )^{2}+1 \right ]^{-4}$

If we define the functions $f$, $g$ and $h$ that map $R$ into $R$ by :

$f(x)=x^{4}, g(x)= \sqrt{x^{2}+1}, h(x)=x^{2}+72$, then the value of the composite functions $ho(gof)$ and $(hog)of$ are given as

  1. $x^{8}-71$ and $x^{8}-71$
     
  2. $x^{8}-73$ and $x^{8}-73$
     
  3. $x^{8}+71$ and $x^{8}+71$
     
  4. $x^{8}+73$ and $x^{8}+73$

Let f and g be the functions from the set of integers defined by $f(x) = 2x+3$ and $g(x) =3x+2$. Then the composition of f and g and g and f is given as

  1. $6x+7$, $6x+11$
     
  2. $6x+11$, $6x+7$
     
  3. $5x+5$, $5x+5$
     
  4. None of the above

Define $f(n)=\frac{n}{2}+\frac{1-(-1)^{n}}{4}$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Thus, $f: \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z}$ the set of all integers. Which is correct?

  1. $f$ is not a function from $\mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ because $\frac{n}{2} \notin \mathbb{Z}$.
     
  2. $\mathrm{f}$ is a function and is not onto but is one-to-one.
     
  3. $f$ is a function and is not onto and not one-to-one
     
  4. $f$ is a function and is onto but not one-to-one.
